description_en: Evaluating one's own actions, recognizing personal flaws, and taking responsibility for self-improvement.
Intellect as a divine trust and test, the faculty distinguishing humans from animals, and purposeful living.
Guiding others towards virtue, sharing beneficial reminders, and earning reward equal to the doer.
Contrasting temporary worldly assistance with everlasting salvation in the Akhirah.
The necessity of digesting and practicing knowledge rather than merely accumulating passive information.

name_en: Minding One's Affairs (Tark Ma La Ya'nih)
description_en: Excellence in faith demonstrated by self-restraint and avoiding unnecessary interference in what does not concern one.
Straightening and aligning rows in prayer as an integral element of worship and communal order.
Living as an embodiment of Islamic values before society while maintaining consciousness of divine watch.
The transcendent weight, solemnity, and decisive nature of divine revelation.
The historical timeframe, angel of revelation, and linguistic conveyance in clear Arabic.

name_en: Dialogue with People of the Book (Mukalamah)
description_en: Establishing common grounds in communication and acknowledging prior scriptures.
Textual invariance across fourteen centuries and alignment with scientific realities.
The roles of scribes of revelation, Abu Bakr's compilation, and Uthman's official codices.
The preservation of phonetics, tajweed, and oral transmission alongside calligraphy.
Direct engagement with the text, leveraging linguistic affinity with Urdu, and daily practice.
The invocation of Allah's name and His attributes of all-encompassing Mercy (Ar-Rahman, Ar-Rahim).

name_en: Praise and Divine Sovereignty (Hamd wa Rububiyyah)
description_en: All absolute praise belonging to Allah, the Lord and Sustainer of all creations and realms.
Affirmation of Allah's absolute ownership and judgment on the Day of Resurrection and accountability.
Direct covenant reserving all acts of worship and ultimate reliance to Allah alone.
Supplication for divine guidance to the straight path trodden by the blessed, avoiding divine wrath and astray paths.

name_en: Idiomatic Translation and Word Analysis (Tafhim al-Alfaz)
description_en: Sentence-level meaning of Surah Al-Fatihah, grammatical particles (lam, wa), and roots of core vocabulary.

name_en: The Meaning of Ad-Din and Divine Judgment (Al-Jaza')
description_en: Examining the specific Quranic usage of 'Ad-Din' as retribution, recompense, and accountability on the Last Day.

name_en: Active Self-Testing and Memorization Discipline (Hifz wa Tamrin)
description_en: Techniques for learning vocabulary independently, shielding translations to test recall, and group recitation standards.

name_en: Sincerity, Willpower, and Overcoming Learning Barriers (Al-Ikhlas)
description_en: The transformative miracle of the Quran across ages, language backgrounds, and the role of sincere intention.

name_en: Jurisprudence of Recitation and Handling the Mushaf (Ahkam al-Mushaf)
description_en: Rulings on reciting without touching the Mushaf during menses, using barriers/gloves, and distinguishing menses from junub.

name_en: Etymology and Root-Words of Divine Names (Ishtiqāq)
description_en: Linguistic derivation of Bism, Allah, Ar-Rahman, Ar-Rahim, and the superlative weight of Fa'lan.

name_en: The Experience and Reality of Hamd (Haqiqat al-Hamd)
description_en: Hamd as an innate spiritual experience of awe, contemplation of human creation, and universal praise.
Gradual elevation of creation from nothingness to perfection, maternal care, and the sign of 'Alam.

name_en: The Essence of Worship: Humility and Love (Al-'Ibadah)
description_en: The lexical definition of 'Ubudiyyah combining total submission (Khudu') and utmost love (Kamal al-Hubb).

name_en: Exclusive Reliance and Divine Guidance (Al-Isti'anah wal-Hidayah)
description_en: Seeking help solely from Allah and navigating the threefold stages of Hidayah: pathfinding, traversing, and arriving.

name_en: The Straight Path and the Trial of the Pul-Sirat (As-Sirat)
description_en: The earthly and heavenly bridges of Sirat, satanic detours, steadfastness, and avoiding the paths of wrath and error.

name_en: Virtues and Unique Status of Surah Al-Fatihah (Fada'il al-Fatihah)
description_en: Revelation of the two lights, greatest Surah, cure (Shifa), and mother of the book (Umm al-Kitab).
Seeking divine sanctuary from Satan upon commencing recitation and understanding demonic vulnerability.

name_en: Reliance on Allah vs Material Causes (At-Tawakkul)
description_en: True reliance versus mere reliance on material means and beginning all affairs with the Basmalah.

name_en: The Station and Multiplied Rewards of Hamd (Al-Hamd)
description_en: Filling the scales of judgment, gratitude for visible and concealed blessings, and post-ruku' praise.

name_en: Divine Sovereignty on the Day of Judgment (Malik Yawm ad-Din)
description_en: Accountability, the absolute manifestation of divine kingship, and retribution on the Last Day.

name_en: The Covenant of Worship and the Hadith of Dividing Salah (Al-'Ahd)
description_en: The sacred dialogue between Allah and the servant in prayer through Surah Al-Fatihah.

name_en: The Spiritual Map: Sirat al-Mustaqim and Human Categories (As-Sirat)
description_en: The righteous path of prophets and martyrs contrasted with knowledge without action and action without knowledge.
Expiation of sins through consecutive Umrahs and the guaranteed reward of Paradise (Jannah) for an accepted Hajj (Hajj Mabroor).
Fulfilling pilgrimage rites purely for the pleasure and approval of Allah, guarding against ostentation, fame, and double intentions.
Distributing monetary charity and sharing food and Zamzam with pilgrims in need.
Going beyond the minimum for fellow pilgrims -- caring for the elderly and gifting authentic educational literature.
Maintaining constant repentance morning and evening, reflecting upon personal shortcomings, and adhering to the Prophetic tradition of istighfar.
Enduring travel hardships with emotional resilience and remaining steadfast in obedience.
Refraining from arguments and staying conscious of Allah's watchfulness at every moment.
The legal and spiritual necessity of drafting a binding Islamic will to settle all debts and moral responsibilities before departing.
Engaging in continuous supplication, systematically compiling spiritual and life goals into a dedicated personal du'a diary.
Preparing for worship through authentic Quranic and Sunnah knowledge, personal day-planners, and studying verified religious guides.
The doctrinal status of Hajj as an indispensable pillar of Islam incumbent once in a lifetime upon capable individuals.
Performing obligatory Hajj promptly without delaying for marriage, worldly accumulation, or old age, given life's uncertainties.
The establishment of Baitullah by angels during the time of Adam A.S. and its reconstruction by Ibrahim and Ismail.
The sacred status of Makkah as Al-Balad al-Amin, its blessings, security, and multiplication of rewards.
The spiritual superiority of Hajj, expiation of past sins, removal of poverty, and being counted among Allah's delegations.
Foundational establishment of pure Tawheed at the Kaaba, shunning all forms of idolatry and shirk.

name_en: Sanctity and Cleanliness of Sacred Spaces (Taharah)
description_en: Inward spiritual purification from sins and outward cleanliness of the House of Allah for worshippers.
The necessity of accompanying da'wah with sincere prayer for those being called.

name_en: Ease and Moderation in Worship (Rifq & Yusr)
description_en: Avoiding self-imposed hardship and utilizing permissible conveyances in religious devotion.
Continuous glorification of Allah during the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah and the days of Tashreeq.
Ritual slaughter of sacrificial livestock during Hajj.
The mandate to feed the destitute and impoverished from the sacrifice.

name_en: Fulfilling Vows and Legal Pledges (Al-Wafa bil-Nadhr)
description_en: The mandatory fulfillment of personal religious vows undertaken for the sake of Allah.

name_en: Veneration of Divine Symbols (Ta'dheem Sha'air Allah)
description_en: Honoring sacred places, sacrificial beasts, and pilgrimage ordinances as evidence of piety in the heart.
The virtue and command of speaking truthfully.
Strict prohibition of mendacity, deceit, and false testimony, alongside the denunciation of idols.
Legal criteria, timelines, and procedural distinctions between Hajj Tamattu', Qiran, and Ifrad.
The command of Rasulullah to learn pilgrimage rites directly from his practice without human innovation.
Undertaking pilgrimage solely for the pleasure of Allah, completely free of ostentation, pride, or worldly gain.
Rules governing pilgrims prevented from completing Hajj or Umrah due to sickness, injury, or hostility.

name_en: Sacrificial Animals and Fidya for Violations (Hady & Kaffarah)
description_en: Compensatory ransoms of fasting, charity, or sacrifice for shaving or committing unavoidable Ihram infractions.

name_en: Pilgrimage Modalities and Fasting Expiation (Tamattu' & Siyam)
description_en: The legitimacy of Hajj Tamattu' and the substitution of ten fasts when sacrificial livestock cannot be procured.

name_en: Etiquettes and Prohibitions of Pilgrimage (Ijtinab ar-Rafath wal-Fusuq)
description_en: Strict prohibition of obscenity, sinful misconduct, and contentious disputes throughout the sacred journey.
Gratitude for Islam, life and health, and using health for worship and service.
Combining treatment with supplication, reliance and humility before Allah.
Divine nearness and response to prayer, as explained through Al-Qarib and Al-Mujib.
Distinguishing worship from asking for needs, and recognizing dependence on Allah.
Creation and the prophets ask Allah; arrogance prevents supplication.
Connecting acceptance of supplication with obedience and trust in Allah.
The lecturer argues for directing supplication to Allah alone and critiques appeals to the dead.
Strengthening faith through Quran, divine names, reflection on creation and good company.
Avoiding heedlessness and despair while persisting in prayer and accepting different outcomes.
The prayer of Ayyub and the lecturer’s discussion of prayer alongside treatment.
Accepting Allah’s decisions, sincerity, humility, persistence and lawful provision.
Encouraging constructive speech and recitation rather than discouraging the sick.

name_en: Good expectations and protection from whisperings
description_en: Discussion of negative thoughts, harmful speech, hope and Quranic recitation.
Occasions for supplication and the instruction to speak good near the sick or deceased.

name_en: Linguistic and Conceptual Definition of Shifa
description_en: Etymological and practical meanings of Shifa (healing/cure) and its contrast with literal boundaries.
Detailed examination of the six Quranic references mentioning Shifa in various contexts.

name_en: Al-Shafi: The Divine Attribute of Healing
description_en: Understanding Allah as Al-Shafi, recognizing that true healing comes exclusively from Him.

name_en: Spiritual Remedies and the Power of Remembrance
description_en: The impact of Quranic recitation, dhikr, and positive mental/spiritual conditioning on health and disease.

name_en: Prophetic Examples of Shifa Through Du'a
description_en: Examples of healing without material medicine from the lives of Ayyub, Ya'qub, Zakariyya, and prophetic traditions.
Definition of Al-Mudhtarr (the distressed) and how sincere du'a in extreme hardship invokes divine relief.

name_en: Trials as Means of Purification and Sincerity
description_en: Understanding why Allah tests believers with hardships to strip away reliance on others and foster pure sincerity (ikhlas).

name_en: Blessings and Expiation of Sins in Illness
description_en: How physical and mental sufferings, even a prick of a thorn or fever, serve as expiation for sins and elevate ranks.

name_en: Patience and the Sunnah Du'a upon Calamity
description_en: The etiquettes of reacting to calamities with 'Inna Lillahi wa inna ilaihi raji'un' and seeking a better substitute from Allah.

name_en: Acceptance of Divine Decree and Contentment (Rida)
description_en: Embracing trials with absolute trust, avoiding despair, and recognizing tests as part of the earthly trial (Dar al-Imtihan).

name_en: Hamd and Shukr in Times of Affliction
description_en: Praising and thanking Allah in every circumstance, viewing trials as disguised mercies rather than burdens.

name_en: The Four Spiritual Stations of Calamity
description_en: Categorization of human responses to hardship: discontentment, patience (sabr), contentment (rida), and gratitude (shukr).

name_en: Inner Nature of Hamd and Sincere Love for Allah
description_en: Understanding hamd as praise rooted in deep love, gratitude, and recognition of the Benefactor (Al-Mun'im).

name_en: Psychological and Neurobiological Benefits of Gratitude
description_en: The healing effects of active gratitude journaling, positive self-talk, and brain re-wiring via Hebbian learning.

name_en: Tasbeeh and Divine Transcendence in Tribulations
description_en: How glorification (subhan Allah wa bihamdihi) removes anxiety and brings deliverance, illustrated by Prophet Yunus and the celestial hosts.

name_en: Authority and Preservation of Sunnah / Hujjiyyat wa Tadwin al-Hadith
description_en: The theological status of the Prophet's Sunnah as divine revelation (Wahy Ghayr Matlu), the living Quran, and the historical reality of its written preservation from the Prophetic era.
The linguistic and spiritual foundation of moral character, emphasizing that outward conduct is the reflection of internal taqwa and loving for others what one loves for oneself.
The sublime moral perfection of Prophet Muhammad as witnessed by his companions, servant Zayd ibn Harithah, and family.
The life, profound dedication to Hadith, piety, filial devotion, and poverty of Abu Hurairah under the Prophet's tutelage.
Devotion, daily supplication, respectful manners, and service towards parents even when faced with religious opposition.
Good character weighing heavier than any deed on the Scales of the Hereafter, elevating a believer to the rank of those who continuously fast and pray.

name_en: Supplication for Good Character (Du'a Husn al-Khuluq)
description_en: Contemplating inner spiritual beauty alongside physical appearance through the consistent practice of the mirror supplication.

name_en: Linguistic Roots and Essence of Gentleness (Al-Rifq)
description_en: Detailed analysis of the root Ra-Fa-Qaf, signifying compassion, ease, assistance, mutual friendship, and pleasant companionship.

name_en: The Parable of the Believer and Ethical Resilience
description_en: The prophetic metaphor comparing the believer to an adaptable plant bending gracefully under life's storms without snapping.

name_en: Curbing Pride, Ego, and Obstinacy (Takabbur wa al-Ana)
description_en: Overcoming relational rigidity, stubborn self-righteousness, and recognizing supreme greatness solely for Allah.
Choosing gentle responses to disarm adversaries and stimulate personal conscience rather than instigating arrogant defense.

name_en: Prophetic Gentleness in Da'wah and Interpersonal Ties
description_en: Reflecting on Surah Ali 'Imran:159 detailing how divine mercy made the Prophet gentle, attracting hearts toward Islam.

name_en: Humility (Tawadu') and Lowering the Wings of Mercy
description_en: Quranic mandate to lower one's wings in kindness towards disciples, juniors, and maintaining warmth across all social tiers.

name_en: Domestic Harmony and Family Prosperity Through Rifq
description_en: Authentic Hadith of Aisha (RA) declaring that when Allah intends goodness for a household, He infuses gentleness among them.

name_en: Virtues and Scholarly Eminence of Mother of the Believers Aisha (RA)
description_en: Highlighting Aisha's legal jurisprudence, inheritance expertise, medicine, memory, and unparalleled charity.

name_en: Spiritual Forfeiture Incurred by Lacking Gentleness
description_en: Prophetic traditions warning that being deprived of gentleness is synonymous with being barred from all comprehensive goodness.

name_en: Prophetic Forbearance (Hilm) in Responding to Hostility
description_en: The Prophet's dignified composure in answering the verbal abuse of the Jews, enjoining gentleness and forbidding obscenity.

name_en: Immunity from Hellfire for the Lenient and Gentle Believer
description_en: Canonical tradition from Ibn Mas'ud affirming that Jahannam is forbidden for every accessible, gentle, and accommodating person.

name_en: Purifying the Soul from Vices (Tazkiyat al-Nafs)
description_en: The profound personal struggle required to purge deep-seated vices and bad habits from oneself, needing sustained effort and divine aid.

name_en: Ontology and Linguistic Definition of Injustice (Al-Zulm)
description_en: Linguistic root and theological reality of Zulm as placing something outside its rightful place, darkness, and exceeding boundaries.

name_en: The Prohibition of Injustice in Sacred Texts (Tahrim al-Zulm)
description_en: Quranic condemnations of oppressors and the solemn Hadith Qudsi where Allah declares injustice forbidden upon Himself and His servants.

name_en: Exemplary Companionship: Biography and Conversion of Abu Dharr (RA)
description_en: Historical account of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari's truth-seeking journey from Banu Ghifar to Makkah, early conversion, and unyielding courage.
The detached lifestyle of Abu Dharr (RA) in al-Rabadhah contrasted with the cosmos operating upon pristine, balanced justice.

name_en: Categories of Injustice: Physical Abuse and Emotional Torture
description_en: Analysis of verbal abuse, character assassination, backbiting, ridicule, and psychological harm as severe forms of oppression.

name_en: Fulfilling Mutual Rights and Maintaining Family Balance
description_en: Synthesizing parental rights with spousal obligations without imbalance, unjustified favoritism, or coercive ultimatums.

name_en: Invasion of Privacy, Breach of Duty, and Time Theft
description_en: Treating meddling in others' personal space, abandoning primary vocational duties, and carelessly wasting people's valuable time as injustice.

name_en: Personal Hygiene, Resource Stewardship, and Eschatological Accounting
description_en: Nuisance caused by foul odors, wastage of communal resources, and the inevitability of surrendering good deeds on the Day of Resurrection.
